subject: Post-call recap: Beacon Health sprint criteria, open tests, and vendor comparison
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed sprint tests

Emily — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed small-sprint we think will surface the signals you care about. TL;DR: we’ll run three short, comparable tests (model parity, load profile, failover) against the prompt set you shared and produce a side-by-side scoring sheet.

Key pain points we heard today
- Latency variability under burst traffic (impacting clinician UX)
- Unit cost for high-volume summary/triage flows
- PHI/data residency requirements: VPC + audit logs mandatory
- Concern about hallucination rates on clinical extraction prompts

Decision criteria you emphasized
- Latency p50/p95 under the 50–200 token range
- Cost per 1k tokens given expected 300k/mo volume
- Throughput (sustained rps) and warm-start behavior
- Model quality on the clinical prompt set (precision/recall for entities)
- Security posture: SOC2 + VPC/HSM options and log retention policy
- Integration effort (SDKs, deployment options)

Proposed comparative tests (2 weeks total)
1) Model parity: run the 120-prompt validation set across 3 model configs (open-llm variant, quantized variant, ensemble) — measure quality (F1 for entities), token usage, and p50/p95 latency.
2) Load profile: synthetic closed-loop test at 50/100/200 rps for 30-minute windows to observe latency tail and CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Failover + routing: simulate a regional outage and measure automated fallback to a cheaper variant + correctness degradation.

Deliverables
- Filled vendor-eval worksheet (attached) with side-by-side metrics and qualitative notes
- Short demo recording of the load run and KV cache behavior
- Architecture note addressing PHI controls and KMS integration

Asks from Beacon Health
- Confirm the decision committee (you mentioned Rajiv (CTO) and Priya (Head of ML))
- Procurement lead / PO cadence (you mentioned end of June as a target)
- Can you confirm the canonical prompt set folder (I pulled the one named "Beacon_Prompt_Set_v3" from the drive link)?

Next steps
- If that looks right I’ll share the worksheet and a one-hour sandbox slot for 24 May where we’ll run the initial parity test. After that we’ll schedule the load window.

Attachments: beacon-eval-worksheet-v1.xlsx, redwood-architecture-qa.pdf

Thanks again — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed sprint tests

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming priorities and a few clarifications: your summary matches our internal notes. A couple quick items: 

- Decision committee: confirmed — Rajiv (CTO) and Priya (Head of ML) will review the vendor scoring; Finance (procurement) will need a rough Q3 forecast for committed spend.
- Timeline: procurement wants a formal POC outcome by week of 28 June if possible.
- Security: please include explicit data residency language and a SOC2 report (or link) in the worksheet. Can you also include average log retention options (30 / 90 / 365 days) and HSM/KMS integration notes?
- Competitors: we’re also evaluating two other providers; we’d like a metric-weighted comparison in the worksheet (weights: latency 25%, cost 25%, quality 30%, security 20%).

We can take the sandbox on 24 May at 10:00 PT — Rajiv will join the 2nd half. Please send calendar invite and the sandbox instructions (VPN/VPC steps if we’re doing private connectivity).

Also: can you confirm if Redwood can expose token-level cost logs for our finance team (per-request traceability)? That’s a gating item for procurement.

Thanks — looking forward.

—Emily
Emily Chen
Director of Product, Beacon Health
